area: Money out: vendors, POs, bills, expenses

rows.feature: Money out menu on the project
rows.what: The project's Finance tab has an “Expense ▾” menu to raise a purchase order or record an expense; POs are locked while the project is in Draft, expenses are not.
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › Costs (Purchase order · Order from the quote · Supplier bill · Expense)
rows.how: One New ▾ on Money carries a Costs group that also records a supplier bill and orders from the quote. There is no Draft lock: costs can be raised at any stage, and only a completed project refuses a new PO until it is reopened.

rows.feature: POs, Expenses and Bills sub-tabs on the project
rows.what: Three sub-tabs list the project's POs (status chips, a strip of PO value · paid · outstanding · margin variance), its expenses (All · Project · Overhead · Reimbursements, totals strip) and a read-only list of supplier bills.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Costs (one list, Kind chips All · Purchase orders · Bills · Expenses)
rows.how: One list replaces the three, with What · Kind · Amount · Paid · Status · Next step; a bill on a PO shows as its PO's sub-line. The strips' totals became the To pay tile (Owners and Admins only). Bills can now be added, opened and paid from the project.

rows.feature: Open a PO or expense straight from a link
rows.what: The address can name the PO sub-tab and a PO to open and highlight.
rows.v2: Project › Money (?open=<record id>, also &do=approve · pay · sendback)

rows.what: Each money-out sub-tab links to Studio Finance's list filtered to this project (the Bills link drops the project).
rows.v1: Project › Finance › POs · Expenses · Bills › View in Studio Finance
rows.v2: Project › Money › Costs; Company › Finance › Money out (search by project)
rows.how: No link out: the project's Money tab holds all its costs and their actions. In Finance, Money out's search matches project names instead of a project filter.

rows.what: “Create Purchase Order”: a required vendor, line items (description, category, unit price, qty), totals and notes; saved as a Draft or submitted.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Expense ▾ › Raise a purchase order
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › Purchase order (also Company › Finance › Money out › New ▾)

rows.feature: Pick the issuing entity on a PO
rows.what: An entity picker sets which of the studio's legal entities issues the PO.
rows.v2: The PO paper's letterhead
rows.how: There is no picker: a PO takes the signed quote's issuing entity and prints on its letterhead.

rows.feature: Add lines from the quote for this vendor
rows.what: “Add {n} item(s) from quote” and a panel of the project quote's lines, the vendor's own lines first, each with Add.
rows.v1: Create PO dialog › Add {n} items from quote
rows.v2: New purchase order › Add from the quote

rows.feature: Type-ahead from the quote in a line's description
rows.what: Typing three letters in a line shows up to eight matching quote lines; picking one fills description, category, price and qty.
rows.v2: New purchase order › Add from the quote (search the quote's lines)
rows.how: Folded into the Add from the quote picker, which has its own search; a line typed by hand gets no suggestions.

rows.feature: Link a PO line to a milestone
rows.what: A Milestone select on each PO line, when the project has milestones.
rows.how: The PO line keeps a milestone field in its record, but there is no picker yet.

rows.what: Delivery address and expected delivery date on the PO, printed for the vendor.
rows.v1: Create PO dialog › Delivery Address · Expected Delivery Date
rows.v2: New purchase order › Deliver to (the site, to start) · Expected delivery

rows.what: An optional “Billing Address” (where the vendor sends its invoice), shown as “Invoice to” on the vendor's page.
Payment terms picked per PO, with a custom text option.
rows.v2: New purchase order › When the vendor is paid (On sending · 15 · 30 · 60 days · Custom)

rows.feature: Payment due day worked out from the terms
rows.what: On issue, the due day is the issue day (COD), N days after issue (Net N), N days after expected delivery (“from delivery”), or 30 days for any other text.
rows.v2: PO panel › Due
rows.how: Due = the send day + the terms' days. Custom terms work out no due day, and the words print instead. There is no “from delivery” rule and no 30-day fallback.

rows.what: An advance as a percentage or a fixed amount, never more than the total; a standard payment is offered only after the advance is paid.
rows.v2: New purchase order › Advance (No advance · A share · A fixed amount)

rows.feature: Quoted amount and margin against the quote
rows.what: A typed “Quoted Amount (from client quote)” gives “Margin Impact” in the dialog, Quoted and Variance columns in the list, and “Quoted vs Actual” in the detail.
rows.v1: Create PO dialog › Quoted Amount; PO list › Quoted · Variance
rows.v2: New purchase order (the client pays… this PO leaves…); PO panel › Against the quote
rows.how: Nothing is typed. It is worked out from the lines that came from the signed quote (client price vs this PO), and only Owners and Admins see it. The lists have no Quoted or Variance column.

rows.what: An AI check matches PO lines to the signed quote, with fuzzy / AI tags and the variance per line and in total.
rows.v1: Create PO dialog › Compare with quote
rows.how: Lines carry the quote line they came from, so the match is exact; there is no AI comparison.

rows.what: GST is always added at the region's rate, also for a vendor who charges none.
rows.v2: New purchase order › Add GST (from the vendor's Charges GST)
rows.how: GST is added only when the vendor charges GST. It is switched on from the vendor and can be changed per PO.

rows.feature: Submit a PO for accounts review
rows.what: With the studio's “PO accounts review” switch on (default), a designer's PO goes to Pending Review; over the PO threshold or with an advance it is forced into review (also via a per-PO switch); an approver's own PO skips the blanket rule.
rows.v1: PO detail › Submit for Review; Create PO › Save & Submit for Review
rows.v2: New purchase order › Save and submit for approval
rows.how: Only a Designer's or a Manager's PO over the limit (S$5,000 incl. GST) or with any advance waits; one under the limit goes straight out, and an Owner's or Admin's never waits. There is no per-PO review switch, and the maker can take a submission back.

rows.what: Submitting creates a task for each Owner and Accounting member; the tasks close on the decision.
rows.v2: Bell › A purchase order needs approval; Company › Finance › To do › To approve; Project › Money / Overview › Needs your OK
rows.how: No task. Owners and Admins get a bell row (Approve · Send back right in the row) and a To do row, and the Company item counts approvals waiting.

rows.what: Owner / Accounting approve or reject with an optional comment; rejected returns to draft; issuing to the vendor is a second press.
rows.v1: PO detail › Accounts Review Required › Approve · Reject
rows.v2: PO panel / Needs you / To do › Approve and send · Send back
rows.how: One press approves and sends to the vendor. Send back needs a note, and the submitter hears either answer. Admins approve too (1.0's lists left them out).

rows.feature: PO approvals queue in Studio Finance
rows.what: Studio Finance's Overview lists POs pending review with vendor, project, advance, a comment box and Approve / Reject, plus a “n POs awaiting accounts review” alert.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › To do › To approve
rows.how: Each row says who asked, when and why it waits (over the limit · an advance · what it leaves against the quote).

rows.feature: Issue the PO to the vendor
rows.what: “Issue PO” marks the vendor as accepted at once (silence counts as yes), stamps the issue day and payment due day, creates the vendor's link and copies it.
rows.v2: PO panel › Send (WhatsApp to the vendor's mobile with the no-login link)
rows.how: Send opens WhatsApp with the message and link. The PO reads Sent until the vendor answers on the link or the studio marks it accepted. The due day counts from the send.

rows.feature: Email the vendor when a PO is issued
rows.what: The vendor is emailed (po.sent_to_vendor) with the PO number, total and portal link.
rows.v1: Email to vendor on Issue PO
rows.v2: PO panel › Send / Send it on WhatsApp again
rows.how: There is no email to the vendor. The studio sends the PO's link on WhatsApp from its own phone, opened on the press.

rows.what: “Copy Vendor Link” copies the PO's no-login page address.
rows.v2: PO panel ⋮ › Copy the vendor’s link

rows.what: /po/{token}: the studio's logo and name, PO number, project, status, delivery and payment details, lines and totals; an invalid link says so.
rows.v2: /po/{token} (the PO on the issuing entity's letterhead, Download PDF)

rows.what: On its page the vendor can Request Changes or Reject, each with a required note, once; accepting is silent.
rows.v2: /po/{token} › Accept · Ask for changes · Decline
rows.how: The vendor now accepts explicitly too. One answer per send; a cancelled or closed PO says so.

rows.feature: Export the PO as CSV on the vendor's page
rows.what: An “Export CSV” button gives the vendor the PO lines as a spreadsheet.
rows.how: The vendor's page offers Download PDF only.

rows.what: The first time the vendor opens the link, the PO is stamped as viewed and the activity says so.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Costs › PO row (“Viewed {day}”)

rows.feature: Studio told when the vendor answers
rows.what: A rejection sends the studio a notice (po.vendor_rejected) and raises a critical “Vendor rejected {PO}” issue; a change request notifies nobody.
rows.v1: Notification po.vendor_rejected; Overview › Financial Summary › issues
rows.v2: Bell › A vendor answers a purchase order; Project › Money › Needs you; Projects listing › Needs attention; Company › Finance › To do › Stuck
rows.how: Every answer (accepted, changes asked, declined) reaches the PO's maker and the project's members, and changes or a no show as a Needs attention reason and a waiting row.

rows.feature: Edit a PO and send it again
rows.what: “Edit” on a draft, a changes-requested or a vendor-rejected PO; then submit or issue again.
rows.v2: PO panel › Edit / Change it (puts it back to a Draft)

rows.feature: Cancel a PO with a reason
rows.what: “Cancel {PO}” needs a reason and cannot be undone.
rows.v1: PO detail › Cancel; PO list ⋯ › Cancel PO
rows.v2: PO panel ⋮ › Cancel the PO…
rows.how: Only a sent PO with nothing paid is cancelled (the vendor reads the reason), with Undo. A PO with payments is closed short instead, and a Draft never sent is removed.

rows.what: “Delete draft” with a browser confirm; non-drafts must be cancelled.
rows.v2: PO panel ⋮ › Remove the Draft (with Undo)

rows.what: “Duplicate” makes a new draft copy.
rows.v2: PO panel ⋮ › Duplicate

rows.what: A PO closes itself when payments reach its total; “Close PO” closes an accepted PO with nothing owing.
rows.v2: PO panel ⋮ › Close it short… (Owners and Admins)
rows.how: It still closes itself when paid in full. An Owner or Admin can also close it short with a note (what is left is not owed), with Undo.

rows.what: “Activity” lists every step of the PO (created, submitted, approved, issued, vendor viewed / answered, payments, closed, cancelled) but never names who acted.
rows.v2: PO panel › history; Project › Files & notes › Activity

rows.what: “View PO” opens a full-screen preview with Print / PDF; “Download PDF” opens a server-made PDF.
rows.v2: PO panel › View the PO (/projects/{id}/purchase-orders/{poId}, Back to Money, Download PDF)

rows.what: In use: Draft · Pending Review · Approved · Vendor Accepted · Changes Requested · Vendor Rejected · Closed · Cancelled (more labels exist but are never set).
rows.v2: Draft · Waiting for approval · Sent back · Sent · Accepted · Changes asked · Declined · Part paid · Closed · Cancelled
rows.how: New words, and new steps: Sent back (approval), Sent (before the vendor answers) and Part paid.

rows.what: “Upload PO” records an external PO (file, reference, amount, date, vendor name, notes), listed in an “External POs” card with download and delete.

rows.feature: Pay a PO (advance, then the balance)
rows.what: “Record Advance” then “Record Payment”: amount (never above the balance), method, reference, date, notes; ends on “PO fully paid”.
rows.v1: PO detail › Record Advance · Record Payment
rows.v2: PO panel / Needs you / To do › Pay the vendor
rows.how: Only Owners and Admins pay. The dialog shows the vendor's bank and PayNow to copy, takes the transfer's screenshot, and offers Undo now and Reverse later. The advance comes first on its own.

rows.what: “Payment History” on the PO: date, method, an Advance tag, reference and amount.
rows.v2: PO panel › Paid

rows.feature: Record a PO payment from Studio Finance
rows.what: “Record Expense ▾ › Record PO Payment” picks a project, then a PO, then opens the payment dialog.
rows.v1: Finance › Operations › Record Expense ▾ › Record PO Payment
rows.v2: Company › Finance › To do › To pay (each PO's advance and balance) or Money out › Purchase orders › Pay
rows.how: No pickers: every amount owed is already a row with its own Pay.

rows.what: Only in Studio Finance › Purchases › Bills (Owners, Admins, Accounting): upload the supplier's invoice, review and confirm, against a project or as overhead; no approval step.
rows.v1: Finance › Operations › Purchases › Bills › Upload supplier invoice
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › Supplier bill (or drop its PDF on Money); Company › Finance › Money out › Bills › New
rows.how: The project's team can record a bill on their project; Owners and Admins also record overhead bills. Still no approval step.

rows.what: An AI reader (PDF, PNG, JPG, CSV or XLSX up to 10 MB, 45 s) fills supplier, number, dates, subtotal, GST, total and lines, marking unsure fields; the read supplier name is not linked to the Supplier picker.
rows.v2: Record a supplier bill › drop the bill (“Read from the file — check it”)
rows.how: A rule-based reader reads a text PDF in the browser, with no AI and no credits; the read name finds the vendor or offers “Add {name} as a vendor”. A photo or scan is kept but not read, and CSV / XLSX are not accepted (8 MB).

rows.feature: Bill details: number, dates, amounts, lines
rows.what: Invoice no., issue and due date, subtotal, GST (as the document prints it) and total, optional line items, a required supplier and a project or the overhead tick.
rows.v2: Record a supplier bill › form

rows.what: Same supplier and number, or same supplier and amount within 30 days, asks “Possible duplicate bill … Record anyway?”.
rows.v2: Record a supplier bill › Record it anyway?

rows.what: A bill can be the studio's overhead instead of a project's.
rows.v1: Record Supplier Bill › Overhead — not project-specific
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out › Bills › New › Studio overhead (Owners and Admins)

rows.feature: Bill status: Unpaid · Part-paid · Paid · Overdue
rows.what: Worked out from payments and the due day, never stored; a zero bill is never overdue.
rows.v2: Bills · Costs › Status (Unpaid · Part paid · Paid · Overdue)

rows.feature: Studio bills list with View and Pay
rows.what: Purchases › Bills lists every bill (All · Unpaid · Overdue) with Supplier, Invoice no., Amount, Outstanding, Due, Status, View (the document) and Pay.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out › Bills (Status: To pay · Overdue · Paid)
rows.how: The panel has Open its file and Pay; the list adds Project and PO columns.

rows.what: “Pay” on a bill opens the vendor payment dialog.
rows.v2: Bill panel / Needs you / To do › Pay

rows.feature: A bill counts as a cost at once
rows.what: A recorded bill counts as a committed cost straight away (a bill and its PO were both counted).
rows.v2: Project › Money › To pay; Costs
rows.how: A bill on no PO counts at once. A bill on a PO is that PO's money and counts once (only what it bills beyond the PO adds).

rows.feature: A bill's document kept and opened
rows.what: The uploaded supplier invoice is stored with the bill and opened from “View”.
rows.v2: Bill panel › Open its file (/finance/doc/{id})

rows.what: “Record Expense”: description (optional), amount, date, a GST tick, receipts, category, vendor, a reimbursement tick and notes.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Expense ▾ › Record an expense; Expenses › Add Expense
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › Expense; Company › Finance › Money out › New ▾ › Expense

rows.feature: Expense receipts: up to five, browse, drop or snap
rows.what: Up to five receipts (images or PDF, 5 MB each) by Browse, drop or “Snap receipt” (the phone's camera); opened from the row.
rows.v2: Log an expense › receipts (“Take a photo of the receipt” on a phone); panel › Open its file

rows.feature: Drop a receipt on the Expenses sub-tab to log it
rows.what: The whole Expenses sub-tab is a drop target; dropping a file opens the expense form with it attached.
rows.v2: Project › Money (drop → Supplier bill); Log an expense › drop receipts
rows.how: A file dropped on Money now opens a supplier bill, not an expense. An expense's receipts are dropped inside its own dialog.

rows.what: A floating “Log expense” button on every project tab opens Quick Expense (amount, category, note, snap receipt, “I paid out of pocket”); its photo was never uploaded.
rows.v2: Project › Money › + › Expense (camera first on a phone); ⌘K search › Log an expense
rows.how: There is no floating button on every tab. The expense dialog on a phone leads with the camera, and a member's empty search offers Log an expense first.

rows.feature: Expense categories set by the studio
rows.what: Accounts Setup › Expense Categories: the studio adds its own categories and marks each Project or Overhead; with none set, the form links there.
rows.v2: Log an expense › Category (a fixed list)
rows.how: A fixed list (Materials · Site supplies · Transport · Labour · Equipment · Meals · Office · Software · Marketing · Utilities · Other) that the studio can't edit. Overhead is picked per expense, not per category.

rows.what: A “Recurring expense” tick that shows a recurring icon (no schedule behind it).
An entity picker sets which of the studio's legal entities records the expense.
An expense needs approval unless the studio switched approval off or the recorder is an Owner or Admin, whose expenses count at once.
rows.v1: Accounts › Workflows › Expense approval for team
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Costs › Expenses need approval

rows.feature: Approve, reject or partly approve an expense
rows.what: Approvers Approve, Reject (reason required) or Partial (an approved amount and a comment) from the pending card, the row's ✓ ✗ or Studio Finance.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Expenses › pending approval card
rows.v2: Needs you / To do / the bell's row / panel › Approve · Send back
rows.how: Approve, or Send back with a note, both with Undo; the maker hears the answer. No partial amount: a different amount is a send-back with a note.

rows.feature: Expense review sent to a named approver
rows.what: A pending expense creates a task “Approve expense: {label} ({amount})” for the approver set in Accounts › Workflows (else the first owner) and an expense.submitted email.
rows.v2: Bell › An expense needs approval; Company › Finance › To do › To approve
rows.how: No task and no named approver: every Owner and Admin gets the bell row and the To do row.

rows.what: Approvers edit or delete any expense; the recorder only their own while it is unresolved; delete asks to confirm.
rows.v2: Expense panel › Edit · Remove the expense (with Undo)

rows.what: A third track beside approval: approvers verify expenses in a project banner and a studio queue (bulk Verify Selected), or reject with a comment.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Expenses › verification banner; Finance › Operations › Overview › verification

rows.what: A “Reimbursement claim” tick puts the recorder's expense on a claim track: pending, then approved (“Reimbursed”) or rejected; the ✓ ✗ showed to every viewer.
rows.v1: Record Expense › Reimbursement claim; Expenses › claim ✓ ✗
rows.v2: Log an expense › Who paid › I paid — claim it back; claim panel › Pay back
rows.how: An approved claim reads To pay back until an Owner or Admin records the payment back (to the member's PayNow), then Paid back, and the member is told. An Owner or Admin can log a claim for another member.

rows.what: Studio Finance › Expenses lists every expense with a status filter, inline approve / reject and edit / delete.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out › Expenses (Status: Waiting · To pay back · Mine)
rows.how: Members see their own projects' expenses and their own overhead ones.

rows.what: From Studio Finance's project picker, “Studio Overhead” logs an expense with no project (Owners, Admins, Accounting only reach it).
rows.v1: Finance › Operations › Record Expense ▾ › Add Expense › Studio Overhead
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out › New ▾ › Expense › Studio overhead
rows.how: Any member may log an overhead expense.

rows.what: Finance › Vendors (Owners, Admins, Accounting): search, chips All · Suppliers · Brands · Inactive, columns Vendor · Trade · Role · POs · Committed · Outstanding; a row opens the vendor's drawer.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Vendors
rows.how: Chips Active · Inactive · All; columns Vendor · Contact · GST · POs · Committed · Owed · Status. Members see names, trades and contacts; the money columns are the Owners' and Admins'.

rows.feature: Open a vendor from a link
rows.what: ?vendorId= opens that vendor's drawer (the PO list's vendor link lands here).
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Vendors (?open=)

rows.what: Name, company, trade, phone, email, notes and bank (bank, account number masked with a reveal, holder); edited in the drawer.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Vendors › vendor panel › Edit
rows.how: Name, trade (the studio's trades), contact person, mobile, email, UEN, Charges GST, bank, account name, account number, PayNow and notes; no company-name field. The bank details are seen and set by Owners and Admins only.

rows.what: Each vendor is a supplier (paid), a catalogue brand (never paid) or both; payable pickers list suppliers and both.
rows.how: Vendors are sub-contractors and suppliers only.

rows.what: A default markup per vendor, used by the price book.
rows.how: Markup lives on the price book's own items.

rows.feature: Add a vendor from any picker
rows.what: A vendor picker adds a vendor in place (a designer can add mid-PO); a name that already exists selects the existing one; a toast offers “Add details →”.
rows.v2: Vendor field › Add a new vendor / Add {name} as a vendor

rows.what: An Active switch; inactive vendors stay on their documents but leave every picker.
rows.v2: Vendor panel ⋮ › Deactivate (Undo) · Reactivate

rows.what: “View transaction history” lists the vendor's POs, expenses and PO payments, grouped by project.
rows.v2: Vendor panel › Purchase orders · Bills · Paid
rows.how: The panel lists the vendor's POs, bills and payments, but not the expenses that name the vendor.

rows.feature: What the studio has committed to and owes a vendor
rows.what: Committed and outstanding per vendor (all-time, non-draft POs) in the directory, for whoever reaches it.
rows.v2: Vendors › Committed · Owed; vendor panel › Committed · Paid · Owed
rows.how: Shown to Owners and Admins only, with the overdue part. Bills and approved expenses count too, not POs alone.

rows.what: “Merge into…”: pick the vendor that stays, a write-free preview of what moves (POs, expenses, price-book, catalogue and quote lines), type the name to confirm; the duplicate is deactivated and its phone / bank are lost.
rows.v2: Vendor panel ⋮ › Merge into another…
rows.how: The preview covers POs, bills, expenses, payments and the price-book / quote names. The vendor kept takes the details it lacks (phone, email, UEN, bank, PayNow). Undo replaces typing the name.

rows.feature: Studio Finance › Purchases tab (Bills · Purchase Orders)
rows.what: One Operations tab with two pills, Bills and Purchase Orders, each with a count.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out (Purchase orders · Bills · Expenses · Paid)
rows.how: One Money out tab with a kind switch in the address (?kind=); the old addresses redirect.

rows.feature: Studio PO list: status filter and sort
rows.what: A status dropdown with every PO status, newest / oldest sort and a project filter.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out › Purchase orders (Status: With the studio · With the vendor · Done; search)
rows.how: Statuses are grouped by who holds the PO. The search matches PO, vendor and project instead of a project filter.

rows.feature: Filter studio lists by issuing company
rows.what: An entity picker at the top filters every Studio Finance list (POs, bills, expenses) by the issuing company.

rows.feature: Create a PO or expense from Studio Finance
rows.what: “Record Expense ▾”: Add Expense or Create Purchase Order, each after a project picker.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out › New ▾ (Purchase order · Supplier bill · Expense)

rows.what: Finance › Pipeline › PO Pipeline: PO cards in columns Draft · Pending review · Approved · Issued · Closed / killed, each opening the project's Finance tab.
rows.how: Finance's Pipeline was removed and its address redirects to Reports › Finance › Profitability. Money out's Status pill groups POs by who holds them.

rows.feature: Studio money-out totals (PO committed, paid, total expenses)
rows.what: Studio Finance's Overview KPI cards “PO committed · Paid” and “Total expenses”.
rows.v2: Company › Reports › Finance (You owe · Vendor spend · Profit and loss)
rows.how: Finance holds the work only; the totals are in Reports.

rows.what: The working-capital widget shows the total of draft POs with “Review drafts”.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › To do › Stuck (PO Drafts older than a week)
rows.how: Each stuck Draft is its own row, not a total.

rows.what: Studio Finance's Overview lists the ten latest money events (POs and expenses among them), each opening its record.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Activity (per project)
rows.how: Each project's Activity has every PO, bill, expense and payment-out step, but there is no studio-wide feed of them.

rows.what: “You owe” = committed POs − paid, “{n} vendor PO(s) with a balance”; its drawer lists POs with a balance.
rows.v2: Project › Money › To pay tile (presses to Costs)
rows.how: To pay covers POs, bills and claims, with overdue in red, and is shown to Owners and Admins only. Pressing it goes to the Costs list; there is no separate drawer.

rows.feature: Money out card (committed vs paid, POs · Expenses · Bills)
rows.what: A card with a committed-vs-paid bar and the split POs · Expenses · Bills.
rows.v2: Project › Money › To pay tile (hover: committed · paid out); Costs › Kind chips
rows.how: Folded into the To pay tile's hover line and the Costs list; there is no bar or split by kind.

rows.what: Committed PO spend on the project broken down by line category, as a bar and a legend.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Overview › Where costs go
rows.v2: Company › Reports › Finance › Profit and loss › Costs by trade and category
rows.how: The breakdown exists studio-wide in Reports (POs, bills and expenses), but no project shows its own.

rows.feature: What counts as a committed cost
rows.what: Issued POs + approved (or Owner / Admin) expenses + every bill; other screens added POs, expenses and bills differently.
rows.v1: Project › Finance (Overview, PO strip, expense strip, Financial Summary card)
rows.v2: Every money-out figure (Money, Finance, vendors, Reports)
rows.how: One rule everywhere: POs from Sent on (a bill on a PO counts once) + bills on no PO + approved expenses. Drafts and POs waiting for approval are the pipeline.

rows.what: Anyone who opens the project sees the Finance tab: every cost, vendor balance and margin, and every create button.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Costs
rows.how: The project's team sees and raises its records. Totals, margins against the quote and vendor balances are the Owners' and Admins', masked on the server.

rows.feature: “No POs issued yet — Raise a PO”
rows.what: An attention row on the Finance overview until a PO is committed.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Costs (empty line with Order from the quote · Record a bill · Log an expense); Profit tile “No costs yet”
rows.how: It is no longer a Needs you row; the empty Costs list and the Profit tile say it.

notes: Nothing was run in either product; the PO-threshold row (MO-095) rests on reading PODetail.tsx against transformers.ts, where the screen reads the thresholds from a different place than they are saved, so they likely never applied. Skipped as 1.0 dead code: the GRN and Record Delivery dialogs (never opened), the PO Settings GRN switch (saved, read nowhere), the po.vendor_acknowledged email (never fired), the materials-tracking API (no screen), supplementary POs from vendor-side VOs, and the superseded /api/finance/purchase-orders/[id]/send route. Receipt scanning exists only in docs (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-receipt-scanning.md) and is about client payment screenshots, which is money in; 1.0 stores expense receipts but never reads them. Left to the books reader: AI Insights on the POs and Expenses sub-tabs, the Xero sync of bills and expenses, the AP Aging, Vendor Spend and Expenses reports, PO numbering per entity, and profit/margin figures beyond the cost rows here.
